statement: A function $f$ is defined for every real number $x \ne 1$ and satisfies $f(x) + 2f\!\left(\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 1}\right) = x$ for every $x \ne 1$. What is $f(3)$?

choices.misconception: I set up the two equations correctly but eliminated with the wrong sign, getting $3f(3) = 3 - 2 \cdot 2$ instead of $3f(3) = 2 \cdot 2 - 3$.
I assumed $f(3)$ and $f(2)$ were equal, so the equation at $x = 3$ became $3f(3) = 3$.
I solved the system correctly but reported $f(2)$, the other unknown, instead of $f(3)$.
I added the two equations to get $3f(3) + 3f(2) = 5$ and took $f(3) + f(2) = \frac{5}{3}$ as the value of $f(3)$.

hints: Plug in $x = 3$ and see what new input appears.
At $x = 3$ the inner input is $2$, and at $x = 2$ it is $3$ again. The map $x \mapsto \frac{x+1}{x-1}$ undoes itself, so you get two equations in $f(3)$ and $f(2)$.
The equations are $f(3) + 2f(2) = 3$ and $f(2) + 2f(3) = 2$. Double the second and subtract the first: $3f(3) = 1$.

solutions.reliable: At $x = 3$: $\frac{3+1}{3-1} = 2$, so $f(3) + 2f(2) = 3$. At $x = 2$: $\frac{2+1}{2-1} = 3$, so $f(2) + 2f(3) = 2$. Doubling the second equation gives $2f(2) + 4f(3) = 4$; subtracting the first gives $3f(3) = 1$, so $f(3) = \frac13$. Then $f(2) = \frac{3 - \frac13}{2} = \frac43$, and indeed $\frac43 + \frac23 = 2$. Transferable idea: when the inner map undoes itself, substitute once more to get a solvable system.
solutions.elegant: The map $g(x) = \frac{x+1}{x-1}$ satisfies $g(g(x)) = x$. Writing $y = g(x)$, the pair of equations $f(x) + 2f(y) = x$ and $f(y) + 2f(x) = y$ gives $f(x) = \frac{2y - x}{3}$ in general, so $f(3) = \frac{2 \cdot 2 - 3}{3} = \frac13$. Transferable idea: solve the system once in general and the whole function falls out.
